name: synthetic-defects feeds golden-compare the frames it made, with the answers
info:
`synthetic-defects` draws a label, paints a known defect into it,
photographs the result through a camera model, and sends one message
per frame. Each frame carries the golden it was made from
(`msg.golden`, plus `msg.goldenKey` so `golden-compare` prepares that
golden once for the whole run) and the exact ground truth
(`msg.synth`).

So `golden-compare` here needs no golden path: it takes the reference
off the message. The one setting that matters is `workingSize`, set to
2100 here, the synthetic label's long edge. The golden is never
upscaled, so the 1024 default resamples it and its 1-3px strokes with
it, and on the default set that costs more than half the recall. Read the
two debug nodes side by side - `msg.result` is what the node decided,
`msg.synth.expected` is what the frame actually contained. A frame
whose `expected.pass` is false and whose `result.pass` is true is a
miss; the reverse is a false alarm on a part that was supposed to
pass. The preview under `synthetic-defects` shows the defect with its
ground-truth box; the one under `golden-compare` shows what the node
made of it.

The set is shot on a fixed rig (one magnification and stretch, as a
camera on a stand gives), and the function node trains
`golden-compare`'s transform on the first frame of each run - a defect
frame, but one small defect does not move a magnification solve - and
writes it to `/data/golden/synth-transform.json`; every later frame is
pinned to it, as a line is. (The golden message cannot train it: the
frames are shot at the rig's magnification, the golden is not.) On the default set that took clean false fails
from 7 of 24 to 0. `failThreshold` is 0.1 here rather than the package
default 0.3: pinned, the sweep found it free on this set and worth 11
points of recall.

Expect a few misses still. With the pin, `printMissingFraction` 0.5,
`failThreshold` 0.1, the tone check at 0.3 and the speck check (0.3,
fail at 8 specks or one of 48 px), the set scores 86% recall - 94% on
small, medium and large - with 2 clean false fails and nothing in the
wrong place; see bench/synth-findings.md. What is left is the `tiny`
severity (a few pixels across under the camera's blur - a resolution
question) and light scratches, which only show as 2-4 px gaps where
they cross thin type.

To run the set on your own label, put its artwork in the container and
name it in the `Golden` field of `synthetic-defects` (or send the path
as `msg.goldenPath`); the defects are painted into that artwork.

Defaults are 87 frames at 500ms apart, roughly a second each to
generate at 1500x2100 - inject once and watch. Narrow it with the
family and severity checkboxes, or send `msg.families` /
`msg.severities`. A new inject stops the run in progress.

This is a test bench, not a production flow. For scored numbers -
recall per family and severity, false-fail rate, sweeps - use
`bench/synth/generate.js` and `bench/synth/run.js` offline.
